subject.title: Npm-valid package scopes with dots/underscores cannot map to ClawHub publishers

question: Should ClawHub preserve slug-like publisher handles and add verified npm-scope aliases, or make npm-compatible scopes canonical publisher handles?
rationale: Both directions alter the identity used for package publishing and can affect authorization, collision handling, URLs, transfers, and existing publishers; the repository cannot safely infer that policy from validation code alone.

options.title: Use verified scope aliases
options.body: Keep stable slug handles as canonical publisher IDs and permit a unique, verified npm scope alias for scoped-package authorization.

options.title: Allow npm-compatible handles
options.body: Expand canonical publisher-handle grammar to match npm scope grammar, with explicit URL canonicalization, collision handling, and migration rules.

options.title: Keep strict scope matching
options.body: Require affected publishers to rename packages or publish under matching scopes, accepting the migration burden for existing npm identities.

recommendation.title: Use verified scope aliases
recommendation.body: Keep stable slug handles as canonical publisher IDs and permit a unique, verified npm scope alias for scoped-package authorization.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the collaborator who supplied the concrete package evidence and identified the product/security tradeoff requiring an explicit decision.
